topic: PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Study nested hash-threshold rollouts generated by common uniforms U_i, with Z_i(p)=1{U_i<=p}, rather than independent assignments at each treated fraction. For N=3, take Y_1=Y_2=0, Y_3(z)=z_1z_2, q=1/2, and interpolation nodes {0,x,1/2}, x in [1/8,3/8]. The exact covariance kernel is Gamma(p,r)={min(p,r)^2-p^2r^2}/9; with the endpoint interpolation weights it gives variance 4(1-x)/{9(1-2x)}, strictly increasing in x, hence 14/27 at x=1/8 versus 2/3 at x=1/4. Use this only as a legal witness, not as a universal node optimum. The target theorem is a robust exact-covariance saddle over declared bounded beta-order potential-outcome or coefficient classes, jointly choosing nodes and linear weights, with a design-based CLT. LinkedIn's deterministic common-hash ramp is the direct consumer. Require an explicit least-favourable bounded schedule and a computable covariance-aware variance estimator. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Characterize the worst potential-outcome covariance under common-U nesting and solve the resulting node-weight minimax problem; the accepted Chebyshev envelope discarded this dependence. EARLY KILL TEST: Drop if the covariance arithmetic fails, if common-U covariance equals the independent-stage envelope after legal conditioning, or if prior nested-rollout work already proves the same robust exact-covariance optimum and limit theory.

open_problems.open_problem: For nested common-uniform rollout over a declared bounded beta-order finite-population class, characterize and solve the exact minimax saddle that jointly chooses treatment-fraction nodes and unbiased linear weights, including an explicit least-favourable potential-outcome schedule.

source_refs.claim: The paper implements staggered Bernoulli rollout with nested assignments, derives polynomial-interpolation TTE estimators and spacing-based variance bounds, but does not optimize nodes and weights against the exact cross-stage covariance.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: Kallus gives a finite-population minimax-variance randomization framework with design-based-inference constraints, but not nested ramp stages or interference-polynomial covariance.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper optimizes a treatment-assignment covariance matrix for a single-stage HT estimator under one-hop interference by minimizing an MSE upper bound, not an exact multi-ramp covariance saddle.
source_refs.author: Qianyi Chen, Bo Li, Lu Deng, Yong Wang

source_refs.excerpt: Exact optimality for the true monotone-rollout covariance Gamma_P(p) is posed only as an open-ended question.
They do not provide a converse covariance construction or a characterization of the attainable matrices Gamma_P(p)

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted rollout result controls exact risk through an L1 total-variation envelope and proves Chebyshev-Lobatto rate feasibility, but that envelope discards the signs, positive-semidefinite restrictions, and cross-stage compatibility constraints imposed by using one common U_i per unit. Cortez, Eichhorn, and Yu likewise bound covariance terms rather than characterize the worst legal bounded schedule. The verified N=3 quadratic witness shows the omission is material: its exact risk varies strictly with the interior node and differs from an independent-stage surrogate, but a single witness cannot establish the global optimizer. The first missing proof step is therefore a characterization of the attainable common-U covariance image, followed by a legal converse construction that attains its support function against the chosen nodes and weights.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality-form saddle characterization of the infimum over legal nodes and moment-unbiased weights and supremum over the bounded beta-order class of w'Gamma_P(p)w, with a computable optimizer and value, an explicit bounded least-favourable schedule, and either an optimality certificate or a regime-stated counterexample to Chebyshev nodes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from industrial safety ramps and unknown interference networks to graph-agnostic polynomial extrapolation, matching the destination problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Platforms ramp treatments through increasing traffic fractions -> interference makes a partial-ramp contrast miss the global effect -> nested measurements identify a low-order response polynomial -> exact common-U covariance should determine the robustly optimal nodes and readout.

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate design as a mixed-strategy minimax variance problem over a structured outcome class and certify optimality using convex minimax arguments while retaining randomization sufficient for inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is also a finite-population minimax design, but its design variables are rollout nodes and weights and its covariance is induced by a common-U path.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate unknown interference coefficients from assignment covariance, optimize the design-side covariance criterion, and construct a legal randomization realizing the optimizer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest network-experiment precedent for making assignment covariance a first-class design object; the new proof must lift pairwise single-stage covariance to cross-stage beta-order inclusion tensors.

open_problems.open_problem: For a node-and-weight rule optimized under exact common-uniform covariance, construct a computable covariance-aware variance estimator and establish a studentized design-based limit theory under sparse or bounded-influence beta-order interference.

source_refs.claim: The common-U rollout estimator is shown unbiased with variance bounds, but the paper gives neither a studentized CLT nor an operational covariance estimator for confidence intervals.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: Chin proves interference-robust CLTs using dependency graphs and Stein's method and proposes a conservative variance decomposition, but for single-assignment HT and difference-in-means estimators.
source_refs.author: Alex Chin

source_refs.claim: Leung proves approximate normality and develops network-HAC inference under approximate neighborhood interference, while isolating the finite-population heterogeneity bias of the variance estimator.
source_refs.author: Michael P. Leung

source_refs.excerpt: The Chebyshev rollout estimator should admit a design-based CLT and Wald coverage result
add either an exact-covariance theorem for Gamma_P(p) or an estimator/inference corollary with a design-based CLT

open_problems.why_unsolved: Every rollout round is a function of the same U-vector, and interference makes each centered round mean depend on overlapping neighborhoods of those uniforms. Thus an independent-stage standard error omits precisely the cross-node terms that drive the optimized risk. Chin and Leung start from one treatment vector or one exposure mapping; their first proof step must be replaced by a vector influence representation for the full signed interpolation statistic indexed jointly by node and network neighborhood. Exact finite-population covariance also contains unobserved cross-potential-outcome products, so the estimator must separate identifiable joint-inclusion terms from a remainder that is only conservatively bounded.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable exact or uniformly conservative estimator of w'Gamma_P(p)w and a theorem that its studentized TTE estimator converges to N(0,1), with asymptotically valid Wald coverage under explicit common-U dependency, bounded-degree or influence, positivity, and variance-nondegeneracy conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the estimator, rollout mechanism, low-order potential-outcome class, and platform motivation whose missing inference layer is the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nested rollout means identify the endpoint contrast -> interpolation gives an unbiased TTE estimator -> common-unit measurements create correlated uncertainty -> covariance-aware studentization is required for operational confidence intervals.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent an interference estimator by locally dependent summands, apply dependency-graph and perturbative Stein bounds, and decompose variance into ordinary and interference-induced components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The common-U statistic is likewise a function of independent unit randomizers with local outcome dependence, but each randomizer affects a vector of nested assignments.

method_exemplars.technique: Use approximate-neighborhood decay for normal approximation and construct a network-HAC estimator whose finite-population bias is isolated as an effect-heterogeneity term.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its oracle-versus-observable variance decomposition is a direct template for separating estimable common-U covariance from unidentifiable cross-schedule heterogeneity.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent a declared design-estimator pair by design matrices and consistently estimate an asymptotic variance bound under complex randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The rollout has a fully known joint assignment law, so the matrix representation may turn common-U inclusion probabilities into a computable conservative variance estimator.

open_problems.open_problem: Under common-uniform nested rollout, determine the covariance-aware minimax MSE design when beta is unknown or the beta-order model is approximate, jointly selecting interpolation degree, nodes, and weights.

source_refs.claim: The paper's low-order rollout estimator makes the degree choice consequential: higher-degree endpoint interpolation amplifies noise, while too low a degree excludes higher-order interference terms; its main theorems take beta as fixed.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: Dette and Wong develop extrapolation designs robust to polynomial-degree misspecification and report large efficiency losses from overestimating degree, but under classical regression covariance rather than nested causal assignment.
source_refs.author: Holger Dette, Weng Kee Wong

source_refs.claim: The two-stage clustered rollout paper derives a concrete bias-variance tradeoff for polynomial-interpolation TTE estimation, but keeps polynomial order fixed and does not solve exact-covariance robust degree selection.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Yu

source_refs.excerpt: A nested Chebyshev rollout schedule can adapt to unknown beta by post-selection while keeping near-minimax TTE risk.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The interaction order determines both the unbiasedness constraints and the oracle node geometry, yet it is rarely known before a production ramp. Classical robust extrapolation treats independent or prescribed regression errors; under common-U nesting, the higher-order approximation bias and the exact variance are generated by the same threshold path and overlapping interference monomials. The first donor proof step that fails is its diagonal information-matrix reduction: it must be replaced by a schedule-dependent covariance functional before taking the supremum over bounded higher-order remainders, and data-driven order selection reuses the same correlated rollout observations used for endpoint estimation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax MSE characterization over a declared bounded higher-order remainder or decay class, with an attaining degree-node-weight rule and either a data-driven selector satisfying an exact-covariance oracle inequality plus uniform coverage or an impossibility theorem and matching adaptation-price lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its low-order polynomial framing makes the opposing misspecification-bias and extrapolation-variance forces transparent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Low-order interference turns ramp measurements into polynomial extrapolation -> the true interaction order is not known ex ante -> overfitting magnifies endpoint noise while underfitting biases TTE -> robust degree-node-weight selection must use exact nested covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct extrapolation designs under polynomial-degree uncertainty through robust optimality criteria and prove cross-degree efficiency guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems estimate a linear functional outside the observed design interval under uncertain polynomial complexity; the required transfer replaces classical regression noise by common-U finite-population interference covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive explicit bias and variance components for polynomial-interpolation TTE estimation under a compound rollout design and compare conflicting design objectives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how rollout choices jointly alter causal bias and variance, which the approximate-beta criterion must extend to bounded higher-order remainders and full common-U covariance.

open_problems.open_problem: Quantify when a finite deterministic shared-hash ramp is a valid approximation to the ideal i.i.d. common-uniform rollout, including its exact covariance perturbation and the conditions required for design-based studentization of TTE.

source_refs.claim: LinkedIn's platform uses an MD5-based hashID, shared by experiments under the same testKey, to keep member assignments consistent as treatment traffic is ramped.
source_refs.author: Ya Xu, Nanyu Chen, Addrian Fernandez, Omar Sinno, Anmol Bhasin

source_refs.claim: The graph-agnostic rollout theory models unit randomizers as independent continuous uniforms and thresholds them across stages, leaving a finite deterministic hash implementation outside the formal randomization model.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a scalable deterministic assignment algorithm and statistical tests for balance, cross-experiment independence, and consistency, but not a covariance error bound for nested causal ramps under interference.
source_refs.author: Qike Li, Samir Jamkhande, Pavel Kochetkov, Pai Liu

source_refs.claim: Golyaev's empirical analysis finds hash-based quasi-randomization quality can depend on the hash function, so deterministic hashing cannot be treated as ideal randomness without a declared condition.
source_refs.author: Konstantin Golyaev

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ideal theory takes independent continuous uniforms as design randomness, while LinkedIn's deployed mechanism fixes a deterministic hash of member ID and experiment identity and maps it to finitely many buckets. Empirical balance tests do not imply the joint cross-threshold inclusion identities needed by exact covariance, particularly for an adversarial finite ID population or repeated reuse of one hash. The first proof step that changes is the identity P(U_i<=p,U_i<=r)=min(p,r): it must be replaced by finite-bucket joint counts under an explicit random-salt, universal-hash, or pseudorandomness assumption and then propagated through overlapping beta-order monomials.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Verifiable conditions on the hash family, salt randomization, bucket count, and finite ID population that yield an explicit operator-norm or entrywise bound between realized and ideal nested covariance, together with the induced TTE risk error and a studentized design-based coverage theorem.

writing_exemplar.why: It establishes that deterministic shared hashIDs are the production mechanism used to preserve member experience throughout LinkedIn ramps.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Large platforms need fast repeatable assignment -> shared hashIDs preserve treatment as traffic ramps -> ideal causal theory replaces hashes by independent uniforms -> finite-bucket hash error needs covariance and coverage guarantees.

method_exemplars.technique: Formalize scalable assignment invariants and validate balance, cross-experiment independence, and enrollment consistency with targeted randomization diagnostics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies the operational invariants a theorem-level approximation to common uniforms must strengthen into uniform joint-inclusion and covariance guarantees.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate assignment-probability and covariance controls through the polynomial-interpolation TTE weights and local-overlap variance expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once hash discrepancy replaces ideal common-U moments, this is the exact estimator and variance proof whose error terms must be perturbed.

literature_map:
Cortez, Eichhorn, and Yu (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2205.14552) are the central anchor: nested Bernoulli rollout measurements identify TTE through polynomial extrapolation, and the paper proves unbiasedness plus spacing-based variance bounds rather than an exact covariance optimum.
The same paper shows why low treatment budgets make interpolation weights unstable and why additional nested measurements have design value, but it supplies no studentized inference theory.
Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn, and Yu (AISTATS 2025, arXiv:2405.05119) derive low-order bias and variance formulas for a two-stage clustered rollout, exposing competing clustering objectives without solving a robust common-U node-weight saddle.
Chen and Li (2024, arXiv:2410.12740) analyze merging ramp experiments under network interference; their independent-experiment variance analysis is a useful contrast to nested shared-randomizer stages.
Chen, Li, Deng, and Wang (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2311.14042) optimize assignment covariance for a one-stage HT design under one-hop interference, showing covariance is a legitimate design variable but not resolving cross-stage polynomial covariance.
Kallus (JRSSB 2021, doi:10.1111/rssb.12412) supplies a finite-population minimax-randomization framework and shows that precision-optimal designs must preserve enough randomness for design-based inference.
Dette and Wong (Biometrika 1996, doi:10.1093/biomet/83.3.667) develop polynomial extrapolation designs robust to degree misspecification, but with classical regression covariance rather than nested causal assignment.
Chin (2018, arXiv:1804.03105) provides dependency-graph and Stein-method CLTs plus a conservative interference variance decomposition for standard single-assignment estimators.
Leung (Econometrica 2022, arXiv:1911.07085; doi:10.3982/ECTA17841) gives approximate-normality and network-HAC machinery with an explicit finite-population heterogeneity-bias interpretation.
Chang (2023, arXiv:2311.06891) develops design-based estimation and asymptotic variance-bound estimation for complex designs, a plausible bridge to a known nested assignment law.
Liu and Hudgens (JASA 2014, doi:10.1080/01621459.2013.844698) establish large-sample randomization inference under two-stage partial interference, but not common-U polynomial extrapolation.
Aronow and Samii (AOAS 2017, arXiv:1305.6156; doi:10.1214/16-AOAS1005) provide exposure-map estimands and observable joint-inclusion-probability variance machinery under known randomization.
Li and Wager (Annals of Statistics 2022, arXiv:2007.13302; doi:10.1214/22-AOS2191) obtain network-interference CLTs under random-graph asymptotics, a different randomness regime from fixed-potential-outcome shared-hash ramps.
Yu, Airoldi, Borgs, and Chayes (PNAS 2022, arXiv:2205.12803; doi:10.1073/pnas.2208975119) characterize graph-agnostic limits for TTE estimation and an unbiased additive-interference solution using baseline information.
Xu et al. (KDD 2015, doi:10.1145/2783258.2788602), Golyaev (2018, doi:10.1515/jbnst-2018-0006), and Li et al. (2022, arXiv:2212.08771) document deterministic hash assignment, ramp consistency, and hash-quality diagnostics; none supplies exact nested covariance or design-based limit theory.
prior_proposal_map:
The current qid exp_rollout_common_uniform_covariance_design contains only state, pipeline, and decision-log scaffolding; it has no earlier proposal core or reviews.
The closest source is the accepted exp_rollout_chebyshev_minimax/tv_envelope_rollout_design bank entry; its proto_core, core, writeup, open_obligations, README, and angle0_v1-v3 reviews were mined.
That entry's oeq:exact-nested-minimax explicitly leaves exact monotone-Bernoulli covariance optimality open because no attainable-covariance characterization or converse schedule exists.
Reviewer angle0_v3 strengthening_paths[3] separately requests either an exact-covariance theorem or an estimator/inference corollary with a design-based CLT.
Its proto_core also preserves follow-on directions for unknown-beta adaptation, dynamic time-by-saturation design, and exact design-based inference.
The accepted exp_design_pm1_exactness_boundary entry supplied an exact covariance-image and implementability template based on symmetrization and reduced slices.
The accepted exp_bipartite_minimax_design entry supplied a dependency-graph CLT and conservative post-design Wald template; its exact-envelope sharpness remains separately limited.
The downgraded exp_commitment_price_coupling entry showed that multi-class productization stops at cross-block kernels, directly relevant because common-U stage covariance is coupled.
The active exp_two_wave_endpoint_poisson_minimax rejected archive and reviews were inspected for least-favourable saddle machinery but concern a different pilot-allocation game.
The downgraded exp_switchback_carryover_adaptation entry was inspected for dynamic-history boundaries; it does not duplicate rollout-node optimization.
